# Results — Study 790 (Composite Equity Issuance)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**Daniel-Titman (2006) composite equity issuance**: the part of 5-year log market-cap growth
NOT explained by a stock's own cumulative return (net equity issuance in log terms) predicts
the cross-section — **high** composite issuers underperform **low/negative** issuers
(buyback-ers). Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. As-of **2025-12-31** (the last complete calendar year; the partial
current year is dropped). Fingerprint `6a1c28a68799` (raw close + adjusted close + point-in-time
shares panel).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Shares | SEC EDGAR XBRL `us-gaap:CommonStockSharesOutstanding` (`dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding` fallback), via the `companyconcept` endpoint; **point-in-time** — the share count as-of each Dec 31 is the latest fact *filed on or before* that date (no look-ahead into an unfiled 10-K/10-Q) |
| Prices | yfinance daily **raw** close (for market cap) + **adjusted** close (total-return leg), resampled to a December-year-end grid |
| Universe | a fixed **36-name** large-cap **survivor** basket (4 of the intended 40 dropped for thin/mismatched EDGAR share facts: META, XOM, WFC, DIS). Current names projected back — **survivorship named on the Signal axis** |
| Signal | `iota = log(ME_t / ME_{t-5}) - log(adj_t / adj_{t-5})`, `ME = shares x raw_price`; splits cancel between the legs, leaving net equity issuance in log terms |
| Sort | each formation year-end, long the bottom-30% (low/negative issuance = buybacks), short the top-30% (high issuance = dilution), **held the next year** (one execution lag) |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* vs 0 on the annual long-short; **Newey-West (1 lag)** HAC *t* (overlapping 5y windows); Wilson interval on the win-rate; 20,000-draw label-shuffle placebo |
| Costs | one-way `cost_bps` x **both legs** x turnover + short-leg annual borrow |

**Survivorship, and its direction here.** The basket is today's large-cap survivors projected
backwards, so firms that issued equity and then *failed* are absent. That biases the sort
**against** the Daniel-Titman claim: the high-issuance survivors we do see are the ones whose
dilution funded growth that *worked* (SBC-heavy compounders, acquirers that paid off). The sign
we find below is consistent with that bias — it is a caveat on magnitude *and* on the sign.

## The headline — annual long-short (long LOW / short HIGH composite issuance)

11 formation years (2014 → 2024), forward-held 2015 → 2025.

| year | long (low issuance) | short (high issuance) | L−S |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2014 | +8.6% | +21.9% | −13.4% |
| 2015 | +16.9% | +39.1% | −22.2% |
| 2016 | +14.6% | +33.8% | −19.2% |
| 2017 | −4.6% | +16.2% | −20.8% |
| 2018 | +25.7% | +52.2% | −26.6% |
| 2019 | +26.3% | +41.9% | −15.6% |
| 2020 | +40.1% | +35.7% | +4.4% |
| 2021 | −15.6% | −24.1% | +8.4% |
| 2022 | +20.2% | +74.8% | −54.7% |
| 2023 | +31.1% | +24.0% | +7.1% |
| 2024 | +27.7% | +20.8% | +7.0% |

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| long (low issuance) mean | **+17.35% / yr** |
| short (high issuance) mean | **+30.57% / yr** |
| **long-short mean** | **−13.22% / yr** (median −15.60%) |
| win-rate (L−S > 0) | **4/11 = 36%** (Wilson 95% [15%, 65%]) |
| annual Sharpe | **−0.69** |
| one-sample *t* (vs 0) | **−2.29** |
| Newey-West *t* (HAC, 1 lag) | **−2.69** |
| label-shuffle placebo *p* = P[shuffled ≥ real] | **0.9972** |

The claimed factor — long low-issuance, short high-issuance — prints a **significantly
negative** spread: high composite issuers **outperformed** low/negative issuers by ~13%/yr,
with |*t*| ≥ 2 in the **wrong** direction and a HAC cross-check that is *more* negative. The
label-shuffle placebo mean is ≈ 0% and the **real sort is beaten by a random relabelling 99.7%
of the time** — i.e. the true issuance→name link is close to the *worst* the shuffle can do for
the Daniel-Titman claim. On this survivor basket the premium does not merely fail to appear; the
data reject it and point the other way.

## Robustness — quantile-width sweep

| tail frac | L−S / yr | *t* | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.2 | −17.59% | −2.34 | −0.71 |
| 0.3 | −13.22% | −2.29 | −0.69 |
| 0.4 | −12.18% | −2.30 | −0.69 |

Stable and negative across widths — the wrong-sign result is not a tail-definition artifact.

## Era contrast — formation year < 2020 vs ≥ 2020

| era | L−S / yr | n | within-era *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2014–2019 | −19.60% | 6 | **−10.16** |
| 2020–2024 | −5.55% | 5 | −0.45 |
| Welch *t* of the difference (late − early) | | | +1.13 |

The significant wrong-sign spread is concentrated **pre-2020** (the mega-cap-growth /
SBC-issuer bull run); post-2020 it collapses to statistical nothing (*t* = −0.45). Even as an
*inverse* bet it is regime-specific, not a stable relationship — the difference test can't
certify the change (*t* = +1.13), so the honest read is "big pre-2020, gone since," not a clean
structural break.

## Costs — one-way × both legs + short borrow

| cost (one-way) + borrow | gross L−S | net L−S | net *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 10 bps × 2 legs + 50 bps borrow | −13.22% / yr | **−13.92% / yr** | −2.41 |

Costs only deepen an already-negative spread. There is nothing to deploy long *or* short: the
long-low/short-high book loses double digits per year, and its inverse is a pre-2020-only,
survivorship-flavoured artifact.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic cross-sectional panel with a TUNABLE planted low-issuance edge; no network;
averaged over 25 seeds.

| planted edge | mean one-sample *t* | mean L−S / yr |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.00 (null) | **+0.13** | +0.81% |
| 0.12 (planted) | **+7.80** | +28.38% |

With no planted effect the sort averages *t* = +0.13 (never a false positive); with a genuine
low-issuance edge it prints a clearly **positive** *t* = +7.80. So the engine recovers the
Daniel-Titman sign when the effect is really there — which means the **negative** *t* on the
real tape is a genuine survivorship-driven sign flip, not a coding bug or a detector that points
the wrong way. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape
stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The claimed premium (long low / short high composite issuance) is
  **−13.22% / yr at *t* = −2.29** (Newey-West *t* = −2.69) — significant, but the **wrong sign**:
  high composite issuers *outperformed* on this 36-name large-cap **survivor** basket. A
  label-shuffle placebo beats the real sort **99.7%** of the time; the win-rate is 36%. The
  faithful synthetic control shows a real low-issuance edge would print a clearly **positive**
  *t*, so this is a genuine **survivorship-driven inversion**, not a hidden sign the tape can't
  resolve. The Daniel-Titman factor that lives in the full CRSP/Compustat point-in-time
  cross-section **does not replicate** on a small survivor basket. **Survivorship is named on
  this axis** and its direction (against the claim) is argued explicitly.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** A wrong-sign spread is no book long the buyback-ers; and the inverse
  (short buyback-ers / long diluters) is a **pre-2020-only** artifact (*t* = −10 early,
  *t* = −0.45 late) that a 36-name survivor basket manufactured — not a relationship you would
  size. Costs only deepen the loss (net −13.92% / yr, *t* = −2.41).
- **Does the published factor replicate here? — BUSTED.** A canonical academic factor,
  replicated honestly on a small survivor basket with point-in-time shares, real costs and one
  execution lag, lands where the desk expects most of them to: the sign flips, the placebo goes
  unbeaten, and the "edge" is a small-sample / survivorship illustration rather than a free
  lunch.
